name: Trimethylaluminium
description: Trimethylaluminium (CAS 75-24-1), commonly abbreviated as TMA, is a highly pyrophoric organometallic compound that is a key precursor in Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) processes for the electronics and solar photovoltaic industries. In PV manufacturing, TMA is used to deposit ultra-thin aluminium oxide (Al2O3) passivation layers on silicon solar cells, significantly improving cell efficiency by reducing surface recombination. In the semiconductor industry, it serves as an aluminium source for ALD and MOCVD processes to deposit high-k dielectric and barrier layers. TMA is also used in the production of modified methylaluminoxane (MAO) co-catalysts for olefin polymerization. The compound is extremely reactive with air and moisture and requires specialized handling under inert atmosphere.
physicalProperties: Appearance: colorless pyrophoric liquid; Molecular Weight: 72.09 g/mol; Boiling Point: 127 °C; Melting Point: 15 °C; Density: 0.752 g/cm³; Flash Point: -17 °C; Vapor Pressure: 8.4 mmHg at 20°C
